Heard Ms.A.Grancy Jose, learned counsel representing Mr.K.Abdul Jawad, learned counsel for the Petitioner, Ms.P.S.Preetha, learned counsel representing Mr.B.Mohanlal, learned counsel for Respondent No.2 and Mr.T.K.Vipindas, learned Senior Government Pleader for Respondent No.3.
2.
The writ petition was filed in the year 2015 challenging Exhibit - P1 order dated 27 March 2015 passed by the Kerala State Human Rights Commission.
The Human Rights Commission, upon a finding that the Petitioner's conduct amounted to human rights violation against the complainant, issued certain directions.

3. Since the order of the State Human Rights Commission referred to the conduct of the Petitioner,
Respondent No.3 was directed to file an affidavit.

Accordingly, an affidavit was filed by the State Police Chief on 29 July 2025 in which the other details pertaining to the litigation of the Petitioner before the Vigilance and Anti-orruption Bureau, the State Police Complaints Authority and the District Police Complaint Authority, Kollam, have been referred to, which read as under:
2025:KER:60892 .4..
"A) A quick verification (QV:No:13/12/SRT) was ordered by Director V&ACB on the complaint of Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai alleging bribery and misuse of official power by the petitioner herein.
It was entrusted to DYSP V&ACB Kollam.
With regard to the enquiry conducted on the allegation of bribe in the complaint, the evidence collected were insufficient to prove the allegation.

sentences.text: However, the Enquiry Officer recommended strict disciplinary action against the petitioner herein for the unjustified act of charge sheeting a case against an innocent person.

Accordingly, the Director V&ACB sent a report to the Principal Secretary to Government, Vigilance Department requesting to initiate disciplinary action against the writ petitioner vide No. T1/21759/2013 dated 28.01.2014.

B) On 24-06-2014, the Inspector General of Police, Thiruvananthapuram Range vide order No A2(a)/2002/2014/TR, issued an Oral Enquiry against the petitioner on the allegation against the Writ Petitioner herein of keeping immoral relationship with the ladies who are residing within Thenmala Police Station limit.
The DySP DCRB Kollam Rural was entrusted with the conduct of the Oral Enquiry.

While the disciplinary proceeding was in progress, on 24-07-2014, the Inspector General of Police, Thiruvananthapuram Range issued another order No A2(a)/8272/2014/TR,
authorising DySP DCRB Kollam Rural, who was conducting the Oral Enquiry against the writ petitioner, to conduct Oral Enquiry on the charge of unjustified act of filing final report against the innocent person by the petitioner along with the charges mentioned in the previous order.

Consequently, the enquiry officer clubbed both the charges and conducted the enquiry and filed the PR 2025:KER:60892 .5..
minutes.

Since the allegation could not be proved in the Oral Enquiry, the petitioner was exonerated of all the charges and reinstated into the service considering the suspension period as service vide order No: A2(a) 2002/14/TR/A2(a)59PR/2014 TR dated 19.12.2015.

C) Consequent to the order dated 11.08.2014 in OP No.79/14 of State Police Complaints Authority, the Office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police Thiruvananthapuram Range initiated an Oral Enquiry against Sri. K S Gopakumar, vide order No. A2(a)- 9669/14TR Dated 26.08.2014.

The alleged charge is that, while the petitioner herein was working as Sub Inspector in Punalur PS, he committed grave dereliction of duty by not registering a case either upon the written complaint of the petitioner Smt. Syamala, or upon her statement.
The DySP, Crime Detachment, Kollam Rural conducted the Oral Enquiry vide Range Office order No. A2(a)- 9669/14TR dtd 04.10.2014.

On completion of the enquiry, the officer submitted a proven PR Minutes before the Deputy Inspector General of Police,
Thiruvananthapuram Range.

The DIG agreed with the findings of the enquiry officer and awarded a punishment of Increment Bar for One Year without Cumulative Effect to Sri. K S Gopakumar vide order No. A2(a)-9669/14TR Dated 24.09.2016.
D) In furtherance of the order dated 01-10-2015 from the State Police Complaints Authority in OP No. 316/2013, the State Police Chief, Kerala issued direction for a Joint Oral Enquiry against Sri.
K.S. Gopakumar, SI of Police and Sri. R. Vijayan, loP.
Subsequently, the DIG TVM Range ordered the Joint Oral Enquiry vide Order No. A2(a)- 16456/2015/TR dated 04.01.2016 authorising 2025:KER:60892 .6..
DySP, Dist SB, Kollam Rural as the enquiry officer.

Illegal detention of Smt. Mable alias Bincey Alex and imposing false charges against her based on the statement of one P V Thomas in Crime No.
1385/2013 U/s 294(b), 324 and 308 IPC, of Punalur PS were the alleged charges against the delinquent officers.
In the meantime, Sri. Gopakumar K S was promoted as Inspector of Police.
The enquiry officer submitted the enquiry report through proper channel to the IGP, South Zone.

Thereafter, the petitioner herein submitted an appeal before the ADGP (L&O) and the appellate authority modified the punishment as 'Censure'
and disposed of the appeal petition vide order No C- 10068/2021/LO dated 06-04-2022.

E) In connection with the registration, investigation and charge sheet of two crime cases in Punalur Police Station (Cr. 1936/2011, & Cr. 1942/2011), and subsequent acquittal of him by the trial Court,
Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai filed two complaints before the District Police Complaint Authority,
Kollam as No 96/2012 and 84/2014, questioning the official act of the petitioner Sri. K.S.
Gopakumar, and Sri. Manjulal, then SI of Police, Punalur PS respectively. The Hon'ble District Police Complaint Authority heard both the parties upon the petition and ordered in favour of Sri.
Muraleedharan Pillai and recommended to initiate disciplinary proceedings against the Sri. K.S.
Gopakumar, and Sri. Manjulal, then SIs of Police, Punalur PS.

The orders recommending disciplinary action against the delinquent Officers issued 2025:KER:60892 .7..
by the District Police Complaint Authority Kollam in petition No 96/2012 and 84/2014 were received at the Office of the District Police Chief Kollam Rural and were forwarded to the office of the Deputy Inspector General of Police Thiruvananthapuram Range for taking disciplinary proceedings vide Letter No G3(a)-29109/2022/QR dated 06-08-2022.

Subsequently, the Deputy Inspector General of Police, Thiruvananthapuram Range forwarded the communication to the Inspector General of Police, South zone for initiating disciplinary action against the delinquent officers vide No. A2(a)-11099/2022/TR dated 15.10.2022.

Meanwhile, the delinquent Officers filed writ petitions before the Hon'ble High Court as WPC 41815/2022, & WPC 3976/2023 and the Hon'ble Court stayed all further proceedings of the orders from the District Police Complaint Authority, Kollam in petition No 96/2012 and 84/2014.

F) Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai filed another complaint as No 18/2016 against the petitioner herein before the District Police Complaint Authority Kollam levelling allegations in connection with the registration, investigation and filing of the charge sheet of yet another case in Cr No. 1486/2012 U/s 420, 120(b), 419, 465, 468, 471 & 34 IPC against him.

The said crime case was registered by Sri. K S Gopakumar, the then SI of Police Punalur Police Station, on the strength of statement given by the complainant one Abdul Salam, S/o Pareethu Kunju, Malika Veedu, Near Punalur Power House against Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai.

The investigation was partly done by Sri K S Gopakumar and there after Sri. T S Sivaprakash, the then SI of Police, Punalur Police Station completed the investigation and the case was charge sheeted on 02.08.2014.

Meanwhile, Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai lodged 2025:KER:60892 .8..
another complaint before the State Police Chief Kerala against the investigation of the aforesaid case and the State Police Chief ordered further Investigation of the case by Crime Branch vide order No D5-81053/2018/PHQ dated 26.05.2018.

During the course of investigation Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai was exempted from the array of accused due to lack of sufficient evidence against him and the case was charge sheeted against the remaining accused before the Hon'ble JFMC II Punalur by the Detective Inspector-V, Crime Branch Kollam on 27.01.2023 and the case is pending trial before the K.S.Gopakumar vs The Kerala State Human Rights ...

4 Hon'ble Court.

Meanwhile, the District Police Complaint Authority Kollam upon the said compliant filed by Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai, heard both the parties and found that the Sri K SGopakumar abused his official powers along with Sri. T S Sivaprakash, the then SI of Police Punalur Police Station and they had taken revenge against Sri. Muraleedharan Pillai.
The Authority recommended for disciplinary action against both the aforesaid officers.
Subsequently, office of the Deputy Inspector General Police Thiruvananthapuram Range initiated disciplinary action against the petitioner vide order No A2(a)-17742/2022/TR dated 01.03.2023.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police, Punalur, Kollam Rural was authorised to conduct the joint Non Oral Enquiry as empowered under rule 8(1)(iii) of KPDIP & A Rules.

Subsequently, the delinquent Officer had filed a writ petition before the Hon'ble High Court as WP(C) No: 7256/2023, and consequently the Hon'bie Court stayed all further proceedings in the order of the District Police Complaint Authority, Kollam in petition No 18/2016 .

G) While the petitioner, Sri. K. S. Gopakumar, was working as Sub-Inspector of Punalur Police Station, he had 2025:KER:60892 .9..
committed grave dereliction of duty while registering a case in Crime No. 687/2012 U/s 498A and 34 IPC.
Consequently, disciplinary proceedings was initiated against him as Non-OE vide Office Order No. H1/16881/12-QR dated 19-02-2013.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police, District Special Branch, Kollam Rural, conducted the enquiry and submitted proven PR minutes.
On the basis of the findings of the Enquiry Officer, Sri. K. S. Gopakumar was awarded with a 'Censure' vide Office Order No. H1/PR/28/12/QR dated 06-01-2014 by DPC Kollam Rural.

H) Another disciplinary proceedings initiated against Sri. K. S. Gopakumar was for non registration of a case at Punalur PS on the complaint received from Mrs Shija, Ms Sreeja, and Mr Prathyush of Panangad Theertham in Punalur on 05/01/2014.

The accused persons while traveling in an autorikshaw bearing Reg No KL 25 4781 hit on a car bearing Reg No KL 25 B 2942 travelled by the complainant and witnesses at Thamarappally Jn on the Punalur - Edamon road.
Consequently, both the parties engaged in an argument.

During the course of the dispute, the accused persons slapped,
abused, pulled the first witness from the car, hit her on the head with a helmet and teared her churidhar.
When the complainant of the case tried to prevent the attack, the accused kicked her in public.
Though the petitioner had recorded the statement on the same day, no crime case was registered against the accused on that day.

The case was registered on 06-01-2014 as Crime No.
28/2014 U/s 341, 323, 324, 325, 354, 427 r/w 34 IPC and without conducting proper investigation deleted the relevant sections 354 and 325 IPC and filed a report before the Hon'bie Court in a hurry.

He did not record the 2025:KER:60892 .10..
arrest of the accused despite being present in the Police Station.
As such, he had committed a grave dereliction of his duty.
Consequently, disciplinary proceedings were initiated against him as Non-OE vide Office Order No. H1/6303/2014-QR dated 10-03-2014.

The Deputy Superintendent of Police,
DCRB, Kollam Rural, conducted the enquiry and submitted proven PR minutes.

Upon the findings of the Enquiry Officer, Sri. K. S. Gopakumar was awarded with a punishment of Increment Bar for Two Years without Cumulative Effect vide order No. H1/PR/21/2014/QR dated 04-03-2015 of DPC Kollam Rural.

sentences.text: It is also pertinent to note that, while Sri K. S. Gopakumar was serving as the Station House Officer (SHO) of Punalur Police Station, the Chairman and Member of the State Police Compliance Authority inspected the Police Station on 25/07/2012.
Subsequent to the inspection, Chairman asked for a report from the SHO.
The Chairman on perusal of the report observed that the report is highly irregular and did not reflect the duties and responsibilities expected from a Station House Officer.
Consequently, the State Police Chief was directed to initiate disciplinary action against the writ petitioner herein for dereliction of duty and breach of discipline.
In pursuance to that, a Non-OE was ordered against him vide Order No. H1/32592/2014-QR dated 05-12-2014 of DPC Kollam Rural.
The Deputy Superintendent of Police, Kottarakkara, was instructed to conduct the enquiry and submit the PR Minutes as per KPDIP & A Rules.
Accordingly, upon the findings of the Enquiry Officer, Sri. K. S. Gopakumar was awarded with a recorded warning under vide Office order No: H1/PR/39/2015/QR dated 16-11-2015 of DPC Kollam Rural.

It is submitted that the general reputation of the officer in handling law and order duties were found unsatisfactory, as many complaints have been received as narrated above, and he continued to involve in such official disputes despite the departmental corrections/measures taken by the disciplinary authorities.
He is currently posted at Police Training College a post of nonsensitive nature, requiring less public interactions."
4. Faced with this affidavit, the learned counsel for the Petitioner, who had taken time to take instructions, states that the Petitioner may be permitted to withdraw the writ petition.
5. The writ petition is accordingly dismissed as withdrawn.
6. The order of the Human Rights Commission thus stands confirmed.
